who: History dissertation committee chair at Louisiana State University in 2006.

evidence.says: James Matthew Mac Donald's 2006 history dissertation on Griffith Rutherford lists Mark Thompson as committee chair.
The first candidate is the author of A Paper House and The White War, with a Cambridge PhD in social sciences.
The second candidate is Mark Louis Thompson, author of Steamboats and Sailors of the Great Lakes and Presque Isle County.

notes: The supervisor's name and LSU role are confirmed, but no sufficiently specific biographical link to either candidate was established. Leave unmatched.

who: Reformation historian R. Emmet McLaughlin, later professor of history at Villanova; PhD Yale 1980.

evidence.says: The faculty list identifies R. Emmet McLaughlin as professor of history, appointed in 1986, with a Yale PhD awarded in 1980.
The reviewed book is R. Emmet McLaughlin's Caspar Schwenckfeld, Reluctant Radical: His Life to 1540.
The candidate Robert McLaughlin teaches history at the University of Hartford and wrote Irish Canadian Conflict and the Struggle for Irish Independence, 1912-1925.

notes: The candidate is the Hartford historian of Irish independence, distinct from the Reformation scholar R. Emmet McLaughlin. The specific Yale supervision attribution was not independently verified.

who: Historian of late imperial and modern China at Binghamton University; PhD University of Chicago.

evidence.says: Yi Wang is associate professor of history, specializing in late imperial and modern China, with a PhD from the University of Chicago.
The doctoral program lists Chuning Xie's The Parallel Family with History: Prof. Yi Wang.
The article identifies Yi-Wen Wang with Urban Planning and Design at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University and explicitly assigns ORCID 0000-0002-8737-0148 to that author.

notes: The supplied ORCID belongs to the urban planning and heritage researcher Yi-Wen Wang, a different scholar from Binghamton historian Yi Wang.

who: James David Miller, historian of slavery and the United States at Carleton University.

evidence.says: The publisher identifies South by Southwest author James David Miller as assistant professor of history at Carleton University.
The candidate authority identifies James David Miller through South by Southwest, published in 2002.
Carleton identifies James Miller as a history faculty member and department chair whose interests include slavery and emancipation in the United States and Atlantic World.

notes: Institution, full name, field and published work connect Carleton's James Miller to the James David Miller candidate.

who: John Anthony Caruso, West Virginia University historian and author of The Southern Frontier.

evidence.says: WVU's description of a 1967 history symposium identifies Professor John Caruso; its personal-name field supplies John Anthony Caruso.
The college newspaper identifies Dr. John Anthony Caruso as associate professor of history at West Virginia University.
The authority identifies John Anthony Caruso as author of The Southern Frontier, published in 1963.

notes: The institution and expanded name identify the John Anthony Caruso candidate. The supplied 1949 doctorate was not independently verified.

who: Verne Elmo Chatelain, University of Maryland history professor, 1945-1965; PhD University of Minnesota.

evidence.says: The archival biography identifies Verne Elmo Chatelain, records a University of Minnesota doctorate, and places him on Maryland's history faculty from 1945 until retirement in 1965.
The authority expands Verne E. Chatelain to Verne Elmo and identifies him as emeritus professor of history at the University of Maryland, College Park.

notes: Name, doctoral institution and Maryland appointment agree, including the student's 1963 date. The supplied doctorate year was not independently verified.

who: Archibald Joseph Christopherson, Cincinnati classicist and ancient historian; PhD Maryland.

evidence.says: The scholarly society identifies Archie as Archibald Joseph Christopherson, a Maryland doctoral graduate appointed to classics and history at Cincinnati in 1965 and promoted in 1968; he directed numerous dissertations.
The candidate is Albert Edward Christopherson, an artist trained at the Royal College of Art and associated with The Gallimaufry.

notes: The candidate artist Albert Edward is distinct from the Cincinnati ancient historian Archibald Joseph. CAMWS dates the historian's PhD to 1965 rather than the supplied 1966.

who: Sally H. Clarke, economic and business historian at the University of Texas at Austin; PhD Brown 1987.

evidence.says: The faculty list identifies Sally H. Clarke as professor in the Department of History, with a Brown University PhD awarded in 1987.
The 2001-2002 fellowship profile identifies Sally Clarke as a UT Austin history professor, Brown history PhD, and author of Regulation and the Revolution in United States Farm Productivity.
The Sally H. Clarke authority cites the farm-productivity book and identifies its author with the University of Texas at Austin; it also records the name Sally Hammond Clarke.

notes: Exact doctoral institution and year, UT Austin appointment and matching book identify Sally H. Clarke among the candidates.
